notes: Batch was routed here as a FIGURES batch, but pages 1126-1137 (Annex D, D.17.1 tail through D.19.3.5) contain NO general formats / syntax skeletons. They carry one table (Table A.3 ROUNDED MODE examples, p1126), prose, and fixed-form COBOL code examples in monospace. All were checked glyph-by-glyph: Table A.3 header row and all 70 cells match exactly (header row crop-verified at 300dpi: '+2.49 -2.49 +2.50 -2.50 +3.49 -3.49 +3.50 -3.50 +3.510 -3.510'); every code example on pages 1131-1137 matches the PDF line for line, including ISO's own internal inconsistencies (p1132 '*> move ir-2 to F' vs p1134 '*> move ir-1 to F' -- both transcribed faithfully) and the odd '. ...' / '. .' continuation glyphs on p1136. Paragraphs that straddle a page break are attached to the earlier page (p1128's opening clause lives at the end of page-1127; p1135's opening clause at the end of page-1134; p1136's at the end of page-1135; p1137's closing clause absorbs page 1138's opening) -- deliberate scaffolding, not loss. NOTE: the p1126 prose says 'The ellipses in the column heading values indicate repetitions of the last digit' but the printed PDF headings carry no ellipsis glyph; the markdown reproduces the PDF exactly, so this is an ISO defect, not a transcription defect, and is recorded here rather than filed as a finding.

findings.pdf_says: D.19.3.3   Object data definitions   [printed at the same typographic level as its siblings D.19.3.1 General, D.19.3.2 Object instantiations, D.19.3.4 Object references, D.19.3.5 Factory objects]
findings.markdown_says: ## D.19.3.3 Object data definitions   [while the immediately adjacent siblings are '### D.19.3.1 General', '### D.19.3.2 Object instantiations', '### D.19.3.4 Object references', '### D.19.3.5 Factory objects']
findings.why_it_matters: The heading is promoted one level, so D.19.3.3 renders as a peer of D.19.3 Objects instead of a child of it, breaking the document outline and any TOC/anchor tooling that walks heading depth. The same promotion recurs elsewhere in this batch: '## D.17.2 Intermediate rounding' (p1126) and '## D.17.3 Final rounding (the ROUNDED clause)' (p1127) against '### D.17.1 General'; '## D.18.2.2 Specification' and '## D.18.2.3 Examples' (p1131) against '### D.18.2.1 General'; '## D.18.3.2 Specification' and '## D.18.3.3 Examples' (p1133) against '### D.18.3.1 General'. In each group only the first '...N.1 General' child kept the correct depth and every later sibling was flattened up one level. No normative text is lost -- this is structural navigation only.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote to the depth of its siblings: in specs/ISO_COBOL.md change line 45695 '## D.19.3.3 Object data definitions' -> '### D.19.3.3 ...'. Sweep the same batch-local instances: line 45298 '## D.17.2', 45326 '## D.17.3' -> '###'; 45431 '## D.18.2.2', 45436 '## D.18.2.3' -> '###'; 45531 '## D.18.3.2', 45536 '## D.18.3.3' -> '###'. The pattern (first '.1 General' child correct, later siblings flattened) appears to run the length of Annex D and is worth a document-wide pass rather than a per-page patch.
